newsitem.title: JAPAN: Foreigners exceed Big Four in Japan stocks - paper.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners exceed Big Four in Japan stocks - paper.

text.p: Stock trading volume via foreign brokerages accounted for 31.1 percent of the total turnover in the first two weeks of 1997, exceeding trade posted by Japan's "big four" brokerages, a financial daily reported on Tuesday.
From January 6 to 17, Japan's four major securities houses accounted for 30.3 percent of total trading volume, the Nihon Keizai Shimbun said.
Even when the Nikkei average shed more than 1,200 points in December, foreign investors were responsible for 28.8 percent of trading activity, it added.
The December percentage was a record for foreign activity in any month, it said
Foreign brokerages have gradually increased their presence in Japan's stock market over the years, but their market share started expanding rapidly from the latter half of 1996.

The paper said foreign brokerages were strengthening their foothold in the Tokyo stock market ahead of planned "Big Bang" reforms. The reforms will deregulate Japan's markets and ignite fierce competition among existing financial institutions.
The increase in arbitrage trading using stock index futures had also helped non-residents expand their business, it said.
The paper said domestic investors were attracted to their sophisticated trading techniques and orders from them were increasing.
It said Japanese life insurers, needing to unload stocks held under cross-shareholding deals, have increasingly sold them through foreign houses.
